impact_scope.description: Reorders where the existing XXHash32 length contribution is added; it does not change the caller-facing API or required call protocol.
Adds a new public XXHash64 hasher implementation and public hashing entry points operating on caller-supplied byte slices and persistent hasher state.
Exercising the newly added module requires compiling/enabling XXHash64 production code, while H0 explicitly enables only base, JSON, and auxiliary JSON modules.

evidence: S0 already contained the public XXHash32 hasher/checksum_u32 functionality changed by this commit.
H0 exclusively initializes and drives JSON decoders and enables only BASE, JSON, AUX__BASE, and AUX__JSON modules; it neither enables nor calls XXHash32.
The S0 gap is therefore limited to the pre-existing XXHash32 portion of the stable changed scope; no XXHash64 entry existed in S0.
S1 retains the unexercised XXHash32 checksum_u32 functionality.
S1 additionally introduces the public XXHash64 hasher and its update!, update_u64!, and checksum_u64 entry points.

Unchanged H0 still compiles only JSON-related modules and supplies input only to JSON decoding paths, so it cannot reach or control the new XXHash64 API, its byte-slice input, or its incremental state.

new_harness_obligation.description: A harness must newly enable/compile the XXHash64 module, instantiate its hasher, feed caller-controlled byte slices through update! or update_u64!, and invoke checksum_u64; varying update chunking would control its persistent buffering/state protocol. None of these actions was possible or required in S0 because the XXHash64 implementation and public entries did not exist.
evidence: std/xxhash64/common_xxhash64.wuffs is a new production file in S1.
It declares a new public hasher implementing base.hasher_u64 and new public update/checksum calls.
H0 has no XXHash64 module enablement, object construction, update call, checksum call, or corresponding input construction.

reason: Within the stable scope of both changed hashing files, H0 already had a material S0 gap because it omitted the existing XXHash32 public functionality. S1 concretely expands that gap by adding an entirely new public XXHash64 module and caller-controlled hashing protocol that H0 cannot compile or invoke. The XXHash32 arithmetic reordering alone would be unchanged internal coverage, but the new XXHash64 public surface supplies the comparative evidence required for AGGRAVATED.
